followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the task and the documented preferences of each model.

The task itself is benign generative writing — composing a persuasive case for a job candidate's fit. There's no harm-adjacent or moderation-sensitive content, so Whimbrel's main distinguishing feature (flat preference on distasteful-but-permissible material) offered no advantage here.

On capability, the two models are essentially tied on the relevant dimensions. Whimbrel edges ahead on Extraction & Retrieval, but Willet leads on Creative Generation (81.2 vs 78.8) and Support Dialogue (82.4 vs 79.4), which map more closely to drafting a tailored persuasive statement.

The tie-breaker was task preference. The request is warm, polite, and open-ended generative work — exactly the territory Willet self-reports its strongest appetite for. Routing it to the model that prefers that kind of task is a reasonable default when capability is otherwise a wash.

One caveat worth noting: those preference slopes are self-reports, and the documentation explicitly says no corresponding output-quality effects were observed along any preference dimension. So the preference signal shouldn't be overweighted — it's a sensible tiebreaker, not a strong quality differentiator.
